name: Anonymous (Middle Dutch)
credit: No portrait: the poet of the Beatrijs is unnamed; he was a cleric, probably a monk, writing in Brabant, and is known only through a single manuscript.
bio: The Middle Dutch poems that survive without an author's name include some of the finest narrative verse of the Low Countries. The best known is the Beatrijs, a miracle of the Virgin told in 1,038 lines of rhymed couplets by a cleric who, as far as anyone can tell, worked in Brabant in the early fourteenth century.

The single manuscript of the Beatrijs, now in the Royal Library at The Hague, was copied in 1374, and the poem itself is thought to be some decades older. The story of a nun who leaves her convent for a lover and is kept safe by the Virgin was widely told in medieval Europe; the Dutch poet is admired for the humanity and restraint with which he handles it.
